sections.html:
Northeast Louisiana's Monroe is both the Ouachita Parish seat and its biggest city, anchoring the second largest metro area in the north of the state. The 2020 count was 47,702 residents, down from 57,597 in 1980, and the 2025 estimate is 46,860. Ouachita Parish had 160,368 residents in 2020. West Monroe, Sterlington and Richwood are the other municipalities in the parish.

The city covers about 31.6 square miles, 3.7 of them water, at 72 feet above sea level, with Bayou Desiard flowing through town and the Ouachita River nearby. Interstate 20, U.S. Highways 80 and 165 and Louisiana Highway 15 reach the city. A home near the University of Louisiana at Monroe or the hospitals is within an easy drive of large employers, which is worth saying to a buyer.

Many older neighborhoods date from the boom decades of the early twentieth century. Pre-war houses can have original wiring, plumbing and plaster, which a buyer will want inspected.

Parts of Monroe have flooded badly. In March 2016, 15 to 20 inches of rain fell across the area over three days, more than any three-day period recorded there before. In Ouachita Parish about 9,500 homes had flood damage and 5,400 were completely flooded, and crews made more than 1,700 high-water rescues.

If your house took water in 2016, a buyer will want the full story. Gather the repair invoices, the flood insurance paperwork and any elevation certificate. If you repaired it yourself, say so and describe what was replaced.

  • Note how high water rose inside the house and what was removed.
  • Keep photos from before and after the repair.
  • List new drywall, flooring, wiring and mechanical work with dates.
  • Be ready to say whether the house has flooded since.

Spring and summer bring severe weather too: heavy rain, hail, damaging winds and tornadoes, including a low-end EF3 that struck the community on April 12, 2020. Roof age and hail history are fair questions from any buyer.

sections.h2: Heat, ice and what they do to a house
sections.html: Monroe is humid subtropical, with over 51 inches of normal annual rainfall and an average of 91 days a year above 90 degrees. Mean daily highs run about 93 degrees in July and August. Winters are mild, with about 35 days a year at or below freezing, and ice or sleet storms are possible. The record low is minus 2 degrees. Long heat and occasional ice are hard on air conditioning, roofs and exposed pipes, so buyers may ask when the cooling system was last serviced and whether attic pipes are insulated.

sections.h2: Which school system serves a Monroe house?
sections.html: Monroe City Schools serves the city limits, with three high schools, three junior high schools and 18 elementary schools. The Ouachita Parish School System is a separate district that includes no part of the city limits, though Ouachita Junior High sits inside the city. River Oaks School has a Monroe mailing address but lies outside the city limits. A mailing address does not settle the district, so confirm it for the specific house and share that with buyers who have children.

sections.h2: Property taxes and homestead in Monroe
sections.html:
Values come from the Ouachita Parish Assessor, 318-327-1300. For payment questions, call the Monroe tax office at 318-324-2536.

The Ouachita homestead exemption lets up to $7,500 of assessed value, which is $75,000 of market value, escape parish taxes. It does not apply to municipal taxes, so a Monroe owner sees the exemption on the parish side of the bill and not on the city side. When you sell, the new owner has to apply for a separate exemption.

Tax topicMonroe rule
Homestead exemptionUp to $7,500 of assessed value, parish taxes only
City taxesNot eligible for homestead
Payment deadlineDecember 31 (R.S. 47:2127)
Interest if lateOne percent per month, noncompounding
Buyer paperworkAssessor's online Sales Questionnaire for a recent purchase

The assessor's website offers a Sales Questionnaire to people who recently bought property. It asks for transaction details so that assessments follow real prices, which means the price in your act of sale may influence future assessments on nearby homes.

sections.h2: What a Monroe sale involves under Louisiana law
sections.html:
A house must be transferred by authentic act or an act under private signature. Under Civil Code art. 1839, the paper has effect against outside parties only from the time it is filed for registry in the parish where the property is, which for Monroe means Ouachita Parish.

You also have to give the buyer a completed disclosure form by the time of the offer, under R.S. 9:3198. If you hand it over late, the buyer can withdraw within 72 hours, excluding weekends and holidays. If you do not know a fact, the form lets you say so, and an honest mistake that was not willful is protected. For a Monroe house, flood history, roof, foundation and plumbing deserve careful answers.

sections.h2: From offer to closing in Monroe
sections.html: After you accept an offer, a notary or attorney orders a title search and your lender sends a payoff. Gather your deed, latest tax bill, flood and repair records and, for a rental, the lease. A financed buyer adds an appraisal and inspection. A cash buyer can close once the title is clear. Taxes, your mortgage balance and recording costs come out of your proceeds at the signing, and the act of sale is then filed for registry in Ouachita Parish. Ask for the settlement statement ahead of time.

sections.h2: What a cash sale leaves out
sections.html:
With cash there is no lender, so no loan approval and no lender-ordered appraisal. Many cash buyers purchase as-is, which can spare you the roof, wiring or drywall work a financed buyer would require. You also skip weeks of showings and the chance of a deal collapsing over financing.

Back taxes, a mortgage and recording costs are still paid from your proceeds. If notices about the taxes were going to an old address, call the tax office at 318-324-2536 before you set a closing date, so the amount owed is known in advance.

A listing suits a house in good shape that can wait for financing and an appraisal. A cash sale suits a house with flood history, an old roof, aging wiring or an owner on a deadline, because the buyer takes it as it stands. A cash offer is usually lower, so compare what you would receive after the payoff, taxes, repairs and carrying costs. Ask every buyer to put the closing date and conditions in writing, and keep copies of everything you sign. If you are an heir or a landlord, bring proof of your authority to sell and, for a rental, the lease with its end date, since tenants affect showings and the date you can hand over keys.

faqs.q: Does the Monroe homestead exemption reduce city tax?
faqs.a: No. The Ouachita Parish Assessor says the exemption applies only to parish taxes, and municipal millage rates are not eligible.
Monroe City Schools serves addresses inside the city limits. The Ouachita Parish School System is a separate district that does not include any part of the city.

faqs.q: How many Ouachita Parish homes flooded in March 2016?
faqs.a: About 9,500 homes had flood damage and 5,400 were completely flooded.

faqs.q: When is Louisiana property tax due?
faqs.a: December 31 each year. It becomes delinquent the next day, with interest at one percent per month.

faqs.q: Do I have to tell a buyer about past flood damage?
faqs.a: The Louisiana disclosure form asks what you know about the property, so past flood damage should be reported. The form has to reach the buyer by the time of the offer.
